title: Priming proof v2: a larger held-out set and a baseline below the ceiling
description:
The first proof (ti-2026-10) had a held-out set of 10 and scored 100% unprimed, so it cannot show labels helping.
Feature: Priming proof v2
  Scenario: A held-out set big enough to read
    Given at least 40 reviewed References per the scope-training rule
    When the operator freezes a new proof id of size 40
    Then each point's agreement moves by at most 2.5 points per disagreement
  Scenario: A baseline below the ceiling
    Given the unprimed classifier agrees with editors on at most 85% of the held-out set
    When the proof runs at N = 0 and each scheduled N
    Then the report can show agreement rising or not, with the held-out size beside it
Constraint: the held-out set is chosen by the frozen sha256 rule, never by looking at unprimed results. If production has fewer than 40 labeled reviews, the work is to gather more editor reviews, not to lower the size.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text: Plan (production has 9 include + 14 exclude labeled reviews = 23; a held-out set of 40 is impossible, and 815 archived references carry no editor label so they cannot be used). Design: stratified 5-fold cross-validation over all 23. Folds assigned by the frozen sha256(proofId, lineageId) rank within each label, so no one chooses items by looking at results. For each fold, the held-out items are scored with a fresh store primed by the first N reviews (review order) of the other folds' items, for N in 0,5,10,all-remaining. Every labeled review is held out exactly once, so each point is agreement over n=23 decisions (N=0 is identical across folds, so it costs 23 calls; about 92 calls total). Report keeps the v1 schema plus heldOut.design. Always-exclude scores 61%, so precision and recall are shown beside agreement. Longer term, a bigger proof needs more editor reviews, which is an editor task, not a code one.
